title: Keep Going, Pass It On
overview: Paul, writing from prison, urges his younger coworker Timothy to stay strong through hardship, hand the message on faithfully, and deal gently but firmly with people spreading harmful teaching.

parts.label: Soldier, athlete, farmer (vv. 1-7)
parts.note: Paul asks Timothy to pass on what he taught to trustworthy people who can teach others in turn, so the message survives beyond them both. Three everyday pictures make the point: a soldier stays focused on his commander, an athlete wins only by keeping the rules, and a farmer who does the hard work earns the first share of the harvest.

parts.label: Chained, but not the message (vv. 8-10)
parts.note: Paul points to the center of his message: Jesus rose from the dead and came from the family line of King David, the line through which a promised king was expected. Paul is in chains like a criminal, but he says the message itself cannot be locked up, so he endures for the sake of those God has chosen.

parts.label: A trusted saying (vv. 11-13)
parts.note: These balanced lines were probably a short hymn or saying already used by early Christians. Sharing Christ's death and endurance leads to sharing his life and rule, and turning away from him has consequences, yet he stays faithful because he cannot go against his own nature.

parts.label: Word fights and a bad idea (vv. 14-19)
parts.note: Timothy should avoid pointless arguments over words and handle the message carefully and honestly. Two men named Hymenaeus and Philetus were claiming the resurrection had already happened, most likely meaning it was only spiritual with nothing still to come, and Paul answers with words echoing the Old Testament that God knows his own people.

parts.label: Dishes in a large house (vv. 20-21)
parts.note: A wealthy home had fine gold and silver pieces for honored use alongside cheap wood and clay ones for everyday or dirty jobs. The point seems to be that keeping clear of corrupt teaching and behavior makes a person ready for good use, though interpreters differ on exactly what one is to separate from.

parts.label: Gentle with opponents (vv. 22-26)
parts.note: Timothy is told to run from the reckless impulses of youth and chase goodness, trust, love and peace with sincere people. He must not be quarrelsome but kind and patient, correcting opponents gently in the hope that God will change their minds and free them from the devil's trap.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether verses 12 and 13 warn that a believer can finally lose their place with Christ, or mainly reassure that Christ stays faithful even when his people falter.
think: When have you seen an argument over words do more harm than good, and what made it different from a disagreement worth having?
